transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08 14:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Silvershore - Head of ML), Samantha Ortiz (Cloud Architect), Evan Park (CTO), Priya Singh (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Silvershore's latency and cost targets, isolation requirements for production inference, and sizing for Dedicated reserved GPU pools. Discussed burst/bandwidth strategy, autoscale/fallback to hosted, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC), and next steps (pricing deck, security docs, benchmark).

Topics:
- Dedicated capacity sizing
- Isolation & networking (VPC, private control plane)
- Burst strategy & autoscaling policies
- SLAs, monitoring, audit logs
- Pilot/benchmark plan and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood. do we have people's roles quick intro?
[00:05] Jordan Lee: yeah i'm jordan, head of ml at silvershore. we own the models and infra planning.
[00:09] Samantha Ortiz: samantha, cloud arch, i'll own the network and security side.
[00:12] Evan Park: evan, cto, more high level oversight.
[00:14] Priya Singh: priya, procurement, i'll handle contracts.
[00:17] Alex Martinez: awesome. priya (turns to priya nair) priya, this is priya nair our se. 
[00:21] Priya Nair: hi all, excited to dig into dedicated capacity and how we can size for your workload.

[00:30] Alex Martinez: to kick off, can you share current usage patterns? e.g. avg qps, latency targets, percent of traffic that needs isolation?
[00:36] Jordan Lee: sure, rough numbers — we run a mix of synchronous user-facing generation and async batch embeddings. avg qps for gen is around 35 calls/sec during business hours, spikes up to 120 for short windows (like earnings days). target p95 latency is under 300ms for short prompts, p99 ideally under 800ms. about 60% of traffic processes PII or sensitive financial pipelines so isolation is important.

[01:10] Samantha Ortiz: on isolation, that means we need dedicated GPUs plus private networking; we can't send data to multi-tenant hosted endpoints for those flows. we also have strict logging/audit requirements.
[01:20] Priya Nair: totally — that's exactly where Redwood Dedicated fits: reserved GPU pools with VPC peering or a private control plane, and we can integrate customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. quick question — what's the frequency of those 120qps spikes? are they sustained or short bursts?
[01:35] Jordan Lee: typically 10-15 minutes bursts, sometimes up to 45 minutes during market opens. the rest of the day is steady but lower.

[01:45] Priya Nair: got it. so a burst strategy we often recommend is a baseline reserved pool sized for sustained qps with burst/overage options or autoscale to a higher tier for short windows. for predictable cost we can do threshold-based burst (reserve N GPUs, allow temporary burst on commit) or use an on-demand fallback to hosted for overflow — but that depends on data residency/stewardship constraints.

[02:10] Evan Park: can you explain the fallback? if we overflow to hosted, does data remain in our VPC? we have constraints that sensitive data can't leave our environment.
[02:20] Priya Nair: good point. fallback to hosted would mean data flows through Redwood hosted endpoints unless you use the private control plane or on-prem option. for strict isolation, the recommended path is Dedicated with burst capacity within your VPC or a private deployment (on-prem) so nothing leaves your network. fallback can be flagged only for non-sensitive routes.

[02:45] Samantha Ortiz: how does networking work — do you support VPC peering or transit gateway? we need to route through our NAT and have strict egress controls.
[02:53] Priya Nair: we support VPC peering, private link options per cloud, and a private control plane for Dedicated. we can also offer an on-prem bundle for air-gapped setups. we'll include architecture diagrams in the security pack.

[03:10] Jordan Lee: on sizing — we care about token throughput rather than just qps. our gen prompts average 350 tokens and completions average 150 tokens. embeddings jobs are larger batch jobs that run overnight. how do you model reserved GPU needs?
[03:24] Priya Nair: we model in token/sec and concurrency. for your 120qps bursts with ~500 tokens total per request, that's ~60k tokens/sec peak. our quants typically recommend X GPUs (redacted in transcript to avoid exact numbers) with continuous batching and KV cache improvements; we'll run a benchmark to validate. plus embeddings batch can run on separate pools scheduled off-peak.

[03:55] Alex Martinez: quick interjection — performance also depends on model choice and quantization. are you planning to use an open model or a larger vendor model?
[04:02] Jordan Lee: we plan to use an open Llama-family model initially, possibly mixed with some L2 vendor models for highest quality. we want to quantify cost/latency tradeoffs.

[04:15] Priya Nair: perfect. we can recommend quantization profiles and batching configs per model; Redwood Optimize will suggest config to hit your cost and latency SLOs. for the pilot we'll propose 2 model variants and measure p95/p99, throughput, and token-cost.

[04:33] Samantha Ortiz: security — SOC2, ISO, encryption, audit logs, SSO. what's supported out of the box?
[04:38] Alex Martinez: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML, RBAC, detailed audit logs per request; for Dedicated we support customer KMS/HSM integrations so keys never leave your control. we'll share the security pack and SOC2 report.

[04:58] Priya Singh: procurement question — what's the term for reserved capacity? annual only, or monthly? and what's the billing model on burst?
[05:06] Alex Martinez: reserved capacity typically comes with monthly or annual commit options; annual gives better pricing. burst can be either pre-purchased burst credits or on-demand overage that bills at higher rate. we'll send a worksheet to help you compare scenarios.

[05:20] Jordan Lee: okay roughly what's the SLA for latency and uptime on Dedicated? we need to show our internal stakeholders numbers.

[05:27] Alex Martinez: Dedicated comes with SLA for uptime and throughput targets depending on the contract tier. latency SLOs depend heavily on model selection and instance sizing; for a properly sized pool we typically see p95s well under your 300ms target on small prompts, p99 under 800ms — but we'll validate with the benchmark.

[05:45] Priya Nair: also worth noting intelligent caching — KV/prefix caching and continuous batching—can reduce per-token cost and improve latency for hot prefixes. we'll include caching recommendations in the pilot plan.

[05:58] Samantha Ortiz: for compliance, we need audit logs shipped to our SIEM and retention for 7 years. can you support that?
[06:06] Priya Nair: yes we can forward audit logs to your account (S3/ELK) and set retention policies; long-term retention might be an add-on depending on storage. we'll include options in the security docs.

[06:18] Evan Park: are there rate-limiting configs per route? we need to protect the model from noisy upstream clients.
[06:24] Priya Nair: yes per-route rate limits, quotas, and token-level throttling are configurable. Redwood Console gives token/call analytics per route.

[06:35] Jordan Lee: bench plan — we want to run a 48h benchmark that covers steady state and burst windows, with our sample prompts. what do you need from us?
[06:42] Priya Nair: we'll need a list of representative prompts, expected qps distribution (by hour), token distribution, and example payload sizes. also network peering info for private control plane. Priya (alex to priya singh) procurement we can do a pilot MSA?
[06:58] Priya Singh: yes we'll need a short pilot agreement and an NDA for data handling.

[07:04] Alex Martinez: ok next steps recap: i'll send pricing + reserved worksheet, security pack (SOC2, KMS notes, network diagrams), and a pilot proposal with benchmark plan. priya nair will own the benchmark and SE work. customer to send prompts and traffic profile. follow-up on 2026-07-15 to review pilot.

[07:20] Samantha Ortiz: one small question — do you support canary rollouts or A/B testing in Dedicated? we want to test model variants without impacting prod.
[07:26] Priya Nair: yes canary/A-B rollout support; you can pin routes to model versions and we support automatic fallback to older variants on quality regressions.

[07:36] Jordan Lee: budget — rough estimate ballpark after this call would help; even a wide range so procurement can prep.
[07:41] Alex Martinez: we'll include ballpark ranges in the worksheet; again annual reserved gives best unit economics.

[07:48] Evan Park: thanks all. if we can validate latency in the benchmark and security is good, we'll likely move forward with a pilot and procurement will finalize.

[07:55] Alex Martinez: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs today and book next call for 7/15.

End of transcript.
